topics.title: Grief Doesn't Need Fixing
topics.hook: The real difference between grief you saw coming and grief that blindsided you, a strengths-based way to hold both, and why adjusting to a changed life is work — hard, honest, ongoing — that comfort accompanies rather than replaces.

bands.label: K-2
bands.title: When You Feel Sad (And Don't Know Why)
bands.hook: A short story and a craft for the days when something got lost — a pet, a toy, a friend who moved — and the sad feelings don't come in any order, and take time, and that's okay.

bands.label: Grade 3-5
bands.title: The Shuffle, Not the Set List
bands.hook: A comparison activity using a music shuffle to show that sad feelings after a loss don't play in order, and getting used to a change takes real time — not one afternoon.

bands.label: Grade 6-8
bands.title: The Map, Not the Schedule
bands.hook: Where the "five stages of grief" actually came from, why even the researcher who named them said not to use them as a checklist, and why "getting used to it" is honest work, not a switch that flips.

bands.label: Teen
bands.title: Neither Kind Is Worse
bands.hook: The real difference between grief you saw coming and grief that blindsided you, a strengths-based way to hold both, and why adjusting to a changed life is work — hard, honest, ongoing — that comfort accompanies rather than replaces.

bands.label: Age 21+
bands.title: The Long Loop
bands.hook: A full adult look at grief as the real, nonlinear work of adjusting to a changed life — expected and sudden loss, a strengths-based practice for the days that still overwhelm you, and a comfort that accompanies the work without pretending to shortcut it.
